description: Correlates k6 load test RED metrics (latency, error rate, throughput, VUs) with PostgreSQL pg_stat_statements performance signals to detect DB bottlenecks under load.

panels.title: Overview — at-a-glance health of the test run and database

panels.description: Current number of virtual users actively running test scenarios.
panels.title: Active VUs

panels.description: Maximum VU count reached during this test run.
panels.title: Max VUs Reached

panels.description: Iterations/sec across selected scenarios — proxy for overall request throughput.
panels.title: Iteration Rate

panels.description: Average % of k6 checks passing. Below 100 % indicates assertion failures or errors.
panels.title: Check Pass Rate

panels.description: Active PostgreSQL connections on the target DB. A spike here correlates with DB saturation.
panels.title: DB Active Connections

panels.description: Total DB query executions per second. Use alongside k6 iteration rate to spot DB call amplification.
panels.title: DB Query Rate

panels.description: Active vs maximum VU ramp. The shape of the ramp drives all load signals below.
panels.title: Virtual Users Over Time

panels.description: Iterations/sec per scenario. A drop here while VUs are stable signals rising latency or errors.
panels.title: Iteration Rate by Scenario

panels.description: 99th-percentile end-to-end iteration latency. A steady climb here while DB I/O rises indicates DB-bound slowdown.
panels.title: Iteration Duration P99 by Scenario

panels.description: Percentage of k6 checks passing per scenario. Drops signal assertion failures or application errors under load.
panels.title: k6 Check Pass Rate by Scenario

panels.description: Data sent and received by k6. Unusual growth in received bytes can hint at query result set bloat.
panels.title: k6 Network Throughput (Sent / Received)
k6 Load Test — RED metrics: rate, errors, duration, VUs, throughput

panels.description: DB connections grouped by state. High 'active' + many 'idle in transaction' = connection pool pressure or lock waits.
panels.title: DB Connections by State

panels.description: Max duration of the longest running transaction. Persistently long transactions cause lock contention and connection exhaustion.
panels.title: Max Transaction Duration

panels.description: Total DB query executions per second from pg_stat_statements. Compare with k6 iteration rate to measure DB calls per request.
panels.title: DB Query Execution Rate

panels.description: Average query execution time per statement. Rising values under stable VUs indicate DB-side bottlenecks (locks, I/O).
panels.title: Avg DB Query Duration

panels.description: Block I/O time (read + write) attributed to pg_stat_statements. A spike indicates disk-bound queries; check for missing indexes.
panels.title: DB Block I/O Time

panels.description: Lock conflicts and deadlocks. A rise concurrent with high VUs signals transaction serialization problems.
panels.title: DB Lock Conflicts & Deadlocks

panels.description: Top 10 queryids by execution rate. Identifies which statements are the most frequent under the k6 workload.
panels.title: Top 10 Statements by Execution Rate

panels.description: Top 10 queryids by avg execution time. The heaviest queries per call — prime suspects for latency under load.
panels.title: Top 10 Statements by Avg Duration
PostgreSQL Performance — connections, query rate, I/O, locks, slow statements
Correlation — k6 load signals vs database impact

panels.description: Side-by-side view: k6 p99 latency vs avg DB query duration. If both rise together the bottleneck is the database.
panels.title: k6 P99 Latency vs DB Avg Query Duration

panels.description: VUs (left) vs active DB connections (right). A linear growth in DB connections with VUs indicates the app opens one connection per VU — a pooling anti-pattern.
panels.title: VUs vs DB Active Connections

panels.description: Rows returned per second from pg_stat_statements. A spike can indicate expensive full-table scans triggered by load.
panels.title: DB Rows Processed per Second
